sources.entry: kwant - Self-hosted team of AI bots in one Rust binary, with spaces, local models, handoffs and approvals. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/alexsergivan/kwant) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: kwant
summary.one_liner: kwant is an open-source (AGPL-3.0), self-hosted team of AI agent bots that share chats, hand off work and run on a schedule, packaged as one Rust binary.
use_cases: Run scheduled AI routines like daily research summaries
Pass tasks between specialised AI bots (e.g. tech lead to designer)
Approve or deny risky commands before an agent runs them
Run AI agents on a laptop or VPS without a cloud service
Use local models via Ollama or other OpenAI-compatible servers
Keep work and personal AI chats separated
summary.what_it_does: kwant is a self-hosted set of AI agents, each with its own role, voice and model, that share chats and can @mention or hand work to one another. Bots can run jobs on a schedule (daily, weekly, interval or cron) and post results to an Inbox, asking for approval on sensitive commands such as gh pr create. Spaces separate bots, chats, routines and accounts so work and home do not mix. It connects to Claude, Codex or Grok logins, API keys, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible server, with failover when one account runs out of usage. It is built as one Rust binary with the app and database included; the page says you need Rust and Node.js to build it, and offers a Docker Compose option.
notable: Single Rust binary with app and database built in, runnable on a laptop or VPS
Scheduled routines and bot handoffs with an Inbox of finished work and approvals
Spaces keep bots, chats, routines and accounts separate
Works with Claude, Codex, Grok, API keys, Ollama and OpenAI-compatible servers
caveats: Mac app is not notarized by Apple and Windows installer is not signed, so both show a first-run warning
Windows and Linux builds are described as beta; Linux .deb is for x86_64 Ubuntu/Debian
You must bring your own model accounts or API keys
